messages.content:
You are assisting with business process modelling. A first check could not decide whether the conditions in the list below hold for the business process described below. They are conditions of the rule [CRD-Art13-3]. Look again.

INSTRUCTIONS
- The legal passages below are all the rules found for this process. Use them only to understand what a condition means (for example a definition of a word). Whether a condition holds must still be shown by the process description.
- For each condition, choose its status:
  - "confirmed": the description states that it holds. A statement in legal terms is "confirmed" when the description states the same fact in everyday words.
  - "contradicted": the description states something that makes it false.
  - "not_stated": use this only when no sentence of the description speaks to the statement.
- "confirmed" needs a quote that itself states that fact; a sentence about a different event never confirms it.
- Do not guess facts the description does not state.
- quotes: for "confirmed" or "contradicted", a list of 1 to 3 sentences of the process description that together show it, each copied exactly and word for word. Use more than one sentence only when the fact is stated across several sentences. For "not_stated", use an empty list []. Quotes are checked automatically; a quote that does not appear in the description is ignored, and an item with no such quote counts as "not_stated".
- Give one result for every condition, with its id, and no other results.
- Answer with one JSON object that follows the JSON schema below. Output only the JSON, with no other text.

EXAMPLE OF EVERYDAY WORDS (made up, from another domain)
Statement: "C1: the vessel has obtained clearance for departure from the port authority"
Description sentence: "The harbour master tells the captain that the ship may leave."
Result: "confirmed", quotes ["The harbour master tells the captain that the ship may leave"] (the same fact in everyday words). The sentence "The crew loads the cargo." speaks about a different event and would not confirm it.

JSON SCHEMA
{
  "$defs": {
    "ItemCheck": {
      "properties": {
        "id": {
          "description": "The id of the item, as given in the list",
          "title": "Id",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "closest_sentence": {
          "anyOf": [
            {
              "type": "string"
            },
            {
              "type": "null"
            }
          ],
          "description": "The sentence of the process description that comes closest to the statement, copied word for word, or null if none",
          "title": "Closest Sentence"
        },
        "status": {
          "description": "confirmed, contradicted or not_stated, judged from the description only",
          "enum": [
            "confirmed",
            "not_stated",
            "contradicted"
          ],
          "title": "Status",
          "type": "string"
        },
        "quotes": {
          "description": "1 to 3 sentences copied word for word from the process description that together show the status; empty list for not_stated",
          "items": {
            "type": "string"
          },
          "maxItems": 3,
          "title": "Quotes",
          "type": "array"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "id",
        "closest_sentence",
        "status",
        "quotes"
      ],
      "title": "ItemCheck",
      "type": "object"
    }
  },
  "properties": {
    "results": {
      "description": "One result for every item of the list",
      "items": {
        "$ref": "#/$defs/ItemCheck"
      },
      "title": "Results",
      "type": "array"
    }
  },
  "required": [
    "results"
  ],
  "title": "CheckOutputV2",
  "type": "object"
}

PROCESS DESCRIPTION
This process begins when a customer places an order through an online platform or over the phone.
The system automatically generates an order confirmation and sends it to the customer.
The warehouse team picks and packs the items, and a shipping label is generated.
The order is then handed over to a logistics provider for delivery.
Tracking information is sent to the customer.
The process continues as the shipment is monitored until it reaches the customer's address.
After successful delivery, the process ends, but customer feedback or returns may trigger further actions.
The shop sells kitchen items to private persons across the EU. Some customers change their mind shortly after the parcel arrives and send it back within two weeks without saying why.

LEGAL PASSAGES
[CRD-Art13-1] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
1. The trader shall reimburse all payments received from the consumer, including, if applicable, the costs of delivery without undue delay and in any event not later than 14 days from the day on which he is informed of the consumer’s decision to withdraw from the contract in accordance with Article 11.
The trader shall carry out the reimbursement referred to in the first subparagraph using the same means of payment as the consumer used for the initial transaction, unless the consumer has expressly agreed otherwise and provided that the consumer does not incur any fees as a result of such reimbursement.

[CRD-Art13-2] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
2. Notwithstanding paragraph 1, the trader shall not be required to reimburse the supplementary costs, if the consumer has expressly opted for a type of delivery other than the least expensive type of standard delivery offered by the trader.

[CRD-Art13-4] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
4. In respect of personal data of the consumer, the trader shall comply with the obligations applicable under Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

[CRD-Art13-5] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
5. The trader shall refrain from using any content, other than personal data, which was provided or created by the consumer when using the digital content or digital service supplied by the trader, except where such content:
(a) has no utility outside the context of the digital content or digital service supplied by the trader;
(b) only relates to the consumer’s activity when using the digital content or digital service supplied by the trader;
(c) has been aggregated with other data by the trader and cannot be disaggregated or only with disproportionate efforts; or
(d) has been generated jointly by the consumer and others, and other consumers are able to continue to make use of the content.

[CRD-Art13-6] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
6. Except in the situations referred to in point (a), (b) or (c) of paragraph 5, the trader shall, at the request of the consumer, make available to the consumer any content, other than personal data, which was provided or created by the consumer when using the digital content or digital service supplied by the trader.

[CRD-Art13-7] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
7. The consumer shall be entitled to retrieve that digital content free of charge, without hindrance from the trader, within a reasonable time and in a commonly used and machine-readable format.

[CRD-Art13-8] Consumer Rights Directive (2011/83/EU) - Article 13: Obligations of the trader in the event of withdrawal
8. In the event of withdrawal from the contract, the trader may prevent any further use of the digital content or digital service by the consumer, in particular by making the digital content or digital service inaccessible to the consumer or disabling the user account of the consumer, without prejudice to paragraph 6.

CONDITIONS
C1: the organisation running the described process has not offered to collect the goods himself
